This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
The appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short), seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case are that on 27.08.2006 at about 9.30 a.m., the claimant was proceeding in a Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-13- 8834 from Gadenahalli Village to Hassan and when the auto rickshaw reached near Gadenahalli Cross down road, the driver of the auto rickshaw drove the same in a rash NC: 2023:KHC:24892 and negligent manner and due to which, the auto rickshaw fell down.
Due to the impact, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries to his body.
Therefore, the claimant has filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
The Tribunal has granted the compensation under the various heads as follows:
Sl . No

. Particulars Amount (in.Rs.)
1. Pain and sufferings 25,000.00 2.
Medical expenses 5,000.00 3.
Loss of amenities

The medical evidence on record depicts that the claimant had suffered fracture to the back bone but there is no evidence that how much amount he has spent for medical expenses and how many days the claimant was inpatient in the hospital.
The claimant, being a NC: 2023:KHC:24892 Government School teacher, is still continuing with the job by maintaining the same salary.
Therefore, the compensation cannot be awarded under the head 'loss of future income due to disability'.
But the Tribunal has awarded lesser compensation towards 'loss of amenities'.

Some amount must have been spent towards incidental expenses like food, conveyance, nourishment,
attendant charges, etc., and that is to be awarded.

Therefore, by considering the overall facts and circumstances involved in the case, it is just and proper to enhance another sum of Rs.35,000/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

6. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.2659/2006 dated 02.01.2012 is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for NC: 2023:KHC:24892 additional compensation of Rs.35,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 93 days in filing the appeal.

iv. Costs made easy.
v. Draw award accordingly.
